research.notes: Wave-3 depth synthesis (verified mid-2026). The economy moves money along three legs: player<->player (trades), player<->game (rewards in, fees out), and game<->studio (treasury). Two amendment facts dominate the design this wave. (1) TokenEscrow / XLS-85 went LIVE on XRPL mainnet on 2026-02-12 (ledger #102204929): escrow now locks IOUs (trustline tokens, e.g. RLUSD) and MPTs, not just XRP — so condition-locked quest rewards and escrow-secured P2P trades can be denominated in your in-game token, provided the issuer enables the token-escrow flag and every token escrow carries an expiration. (2) Batch / XLS-56 is NOT on mainnet — it was disabled in rippled 3.1.1 (released 2026-02-23) after a Feb-19 disclosure of an unauthorized-inner-transaction-execution bug; both `Batch` and `fixBatchInnerSigs` are marked Obsolete / unsupported. A corrected `BatchV1_1` is under review with no release date. Treat atomic multi-op batching (mass payouts, all-or-nothing trades) as NOT-YET on mainnet and design a per-payment fallback. Payment channels remain XRP-ONLY — no token/MPT support — so high-frequency tipping/streaming priced in your in-game token is not directly channel-able; either price tips in XRP or accumulate off-ledger and settle. delivered_amount (renamed DeliverMax in API v2) is the single most important backend-safety field: never credit a player from the Amount field. Destination tags remain the standard custodial sub-account crediting mechanism; X-addresses bundle address+tag for safer UX.

capabilities.name: Atomic cross-currency swap via OfferCreate (Fill-or-Kill)
capabilities.summary: Player-to-player or player-to-game currency trades settled atomically against the XRPL central limit order book (DEX). An OfferCreate is a limit order with TakerGets (what you sell) and TakerPays (what you buy); it can swap any token<->token or token<->XRP. For a game trade you want determinism, not a resting order: set tfFillOrKill so the offer executes only if the FULL TakerPays amount is obtainable in one shot, otherwise it cancels and creates no ledger object. This gives an all-or-nothing single-currency swap without escrow overhead — ideal for 'sell 100 gold-token for 5 RLUSD, now, exactly, or not at all'. tfImmediateOrCancel is the looser variant (take whatever is available immediately, leave no resting offer).
gotchas: tfImmediateOrCancel + tfFillOrKill together is invalid (temINVALID_FLAG) — pick one.
tfImmediateOrCancel can return tesSUCCESS while trading ZERO currency (no match available). Always inspect the metadata / delivered amounts to confirm the trade actually happened — success != filled.

Fill-or-Kill needs the full TakerPays; thin order books mean legitimate trades fail. For player-to-player direct swaps, pair offers won't auto-match unless prices cross — consider escrow-secured trade instead for a guaranteed 1:1 exchange between two specific players.
A swap touching an issued token requires a trust line for that token on the taker side; no trust line means the buy side can't be credited.
This is a market trade against the global DEX, not a private trade — another account can take the liquidity first.

best_for.purpose: Player sells in-game token for stablecoin at an exact price or not at all
Cash-out / on-ramp swap between XRP and the studio's issued token
Guaranteed 1:1 swap between two named players

capabilities.name: Escrow-secured player-to-player trade (token escrow)
capabilities.summary: A guaranteed, non-market trade between two specific players where each side locks its asset in escrow and release is gated on a shared secret (crypto-condition) or a time window, eliminating counterparty risk without a central order book. Since TokenEscrow (XLS-85) activated on mainnet 2026-02-12 (ledger #102204929), the escrowed asset can be an IOU (your in-game token, RLUSD, etc.) or an MPT — not just XRP. Pattern: player A escrows item-token with a PREIMAGE-SHA-256 Condition; player B escrows the agreed price with the SAME condition; whoever holds the preimage finishes both, or a CancelAfter deadline refunds both. This is the right primitive for a 'trade window' that must be atomic-feeling without relying on the still-disabled Batch amendment.
gotchas: TokenEscrow requires the token ISSUER to have enabled the escrow flag on the token; an arbitrary IOU cannot be escrowed unless its issuer opted in.
Every TOKEN escrow MUST carry an expiration (CancelAfter / time bound) — unlike XRP escrow this is mandatory. Plan a refund path.
EscrowFinish with a Fulfillment costs a minimum 330 drops + 10 drops per 16 bytes of fulfillment — pricier than a plain transaction; budget fees for high-volume trade flows.
PREIMAGE-SHA-256 is the ONLY supported crypto-condition type — no other condition logic on-ledger.

Two separate escrows are NOT a single atomic transaction: there is a window where A has finished but B has not. Crypto-conditions reduce this (same preimage unlocks both) but a malicious/absent counterparty can still leave one leg locked until CancelAfter. True atomicity awaits BatchV1_1.

best_for.purpose: Guaranteed item-for-currency trade between two named players, no DEX liquidity needed
Trade window denominated in the studio's in-game token
High-frequency micro-trades

capabilities.name: Conditional quest reward (crypto-condition escrow)
capabilities.summary: Lock a reward (in-game token, XRP, or MPT) in escrow when a quest starts and release it only when the player proves completion. The studio creates an EscrowCreate with a PREIMAGE-SHA-256 Condition; when the backend verifies the quest is done it reveals the Fulfillment (the preimage) so the player can EscrowFinish and claim. FinishAfter can gate a timed reward (e.g. a staking / 'come back in 7 days' bonus); CancelAfter reclaims unclaimed rewards back to the treasury. Combine condition + FinishAfter for 'completable only after T and only with proof'. Post-TokenEscrow this works with the studio's own token, not just XRP.
gotchas: Anyone who learns the Fulfillment (preimage) can finish the escrow — the preimage IS the bearer token. Reveal it only to the entitled player and only after verification; treat it like a secret.
The fulfillment is revealed on-ledger when EscrowFinish is submitted, so a single quest condition reused across many players is burned after the first claim. Use a UNIQUE condition per escrow/player.
Token escrows require an expiration — a never-claimed reward will eventually need EscrowCancel to recover the funds; don't leak treasury into dead escrows.
EscrowFinish-with-fulfillment fee scales with fulfillment size (330 + 10 drops/16 bytes) — keep preimages short.
Escrow ties up reserve and locked funds per object; thousands of simultaneous quest escrows inflate owner reserve requirements on the treasury account.

best_for.purpose: Provably-fair quest/achievement payout released on verified completion
Time-locked staking or login-streak reward
Routine instant rewards with no condition

capabilities.name: Batch reward distribution / mass payout (Batch — NOT on mainnet)
capabilities.summary: XLS-56 Batch would wrap up to 8 inner transactions (min 2) into one atomic envelope with four execution modes — tfAllOrNothing (all succeed or none), tfOnlyOne (first success wins), tfUntilFailure (apply until first failure), tfIndependent (apply all regardless). The dream use case for a game economy is one mass-payout batch ('credit 50 tournament winners atomically') or an all-or-nothing multi-leg trade. STATUS WARNING (mid-2026): the original Batch and fixBatchInnerSigs amendments were DISABLED in rippled 3.1.1 (2026-02-23) after a Feb-19 disclosure that inner transactions could execute on arbitrary victim accounts without their keys. Both are marked Obsolete / unsupported and CANNOT be voted onto any production network. A corrected BatchV1_1 is under review with NO release date. DO NOT design a shipping payout pipeline that depends on Batch today — use per-payment loops with the partial-payment-safe credit pattern as the mainnet fallback.
gotchas: NOT enabled on mainnet — disabled in rippled 3.1.1; the spec is Final but the amendment is Obsolete pending BatchV1_1. Anything built on it runs only against historical testnet builds, not production.
Max 8 inner transactions per batch even when it returns — not a bulk-airdrop primitive for thousands of accounts; large payouts still need chunking or a loop.

Inner transactions must have Fee '0', empty SigningPubKey, the tfInnerBatchTxn flag, and no TxnSignature/Signers; multi-account batches authenticate via BatchSigners. The original bug was precisely in this inner-signature path — verify the BatchV1_1 model before reuse.

Until BatchV1_1 ships there is NO atomic multi-account or all-or-nothing transaction primitive on XRPL mainnet — escrow with shared crypto-conditions is the nearest substitute, but it is not truly atomic across legs.
Track release notes: only treat Batch as available once a rippled release re-enables a Batch-family amendment AND it reaches majority validator support on mainnet.

best_for.purpose: Atomic multi-winner tournament payout (FUTURE, once BatchV1_1 ships)
All-or-nothing multi-leg trade in one transaction (FUTURE)
Production mass payout TODAY

capabilities.name: Micropayment tipping & streaming via payment channels (XRP-only)
capabilities.summary: Payment channels enable high-frequency, near-instant, off-ledger micropayments: the sender funds a channel once, then signs many off-ledger Claims that the recipient verifies WITHOUT submitting a transaction or waiting for a ledger close. The recipient redeems accumulated claims with a single on-ledger PaymentChannelClaim later. Perfect shape for in-game tipping streams, pay-per-second spectating, or continuous creator tips where per-tx fees would dwarf the tip. CONSTRAINT (verified mid-2026): payment channels are XRP-ONLY — no IOU/MPT support, unlike escrow post-XLS-85. So tips must be denominated in XRP, or you accumulate in your in-game token off-ledger and periodically settle. SettleDelay protects the sender: after a close request, funds stay claimable by the recipient for the delay window before the sender reclaims the remainder.
gotchas: XRP ONLY. Payment channels do NOT carry IOUs or MPTs — you cannot stream the studio's in-game token directly through a channel. This is the single biggest constraint for token-denominated tipping.

Claims are signed off-ledger with channel_authorize and verified with channel_verify; security of the whole stream rests on the recipient validating each claim's signature and the running total before delivering value in-game.
Each claim is monotonic — the recipient should only act on a claim larger than the last; replaying or accepting a smaller claim under-credits.
Funds are locked in the channel and subject to SettleDelay on close; over-funding ties up XRP, under-funding caps the tip stream.
Channel setup costs an on-ledger transaction + reserve; only worth it for an ongoing relationship (a creator/host), not a one-off tip — for one-offs send a plain Payment.

best_for.purpose: Continuous / high-frequency in-game tipping to a creator or host (priced in XRP)
Pay-per-second spectating or streaming-content access
Tipping denominated in the studio's in-game token

capabilities.name: Marketplace fee routing to studio treasury
capabilities.summary: Routing a percentage cut of every in-game marketplace sale to the studio treasury account. Because Batch (atomic multi-leg) is not on mainnet, the reliable pattern today is: settle the trade, then in the same backend flow issue a separate Payment of the fee leg to the treasury, tagged with a DestinationTag identifying the sale. For NFT/asset sales specifically, XRPL's native NFT offers carry a built-in royalty/transfer-fee mechanism (the issuer's TransferFee) so a configured cut auto-accrues to the issuer on secondary sales without a separate fee transaction. For fungible-token marketplaces, the issuer's trustline TransferRate similarly skims a percentage on token movement between holders. Combine native fee mechanisms (no extra tx, no atomicity gap) with explicit fee Payments where finer routing is needed.
gotchas: Without Batch on mainnet, an explicit fee Payment is a SEPARATE transaction from the sale — there's a window where the sale settled but the fee leg failed. Prefer native TransferFee/TransferRate (atomic, protocol-enforced) where possible; reconcile explicit fee payments.
TransferRate (fungible token fee) applies to holder-to-holder transfers but NOT to payments to/from the issuer itself — fee routing math must account for who the issuer is in the flow.
NFT TransferFee is set at mint time and is hard to change later — pick the studio's royalty rate carefully before minting the asset line.
Always send the treasury leg with a DestinationTag so accounting can attribute which sale produced which fee; enable RequireDest on the treasury account to reject untagged deposits.
Partial-payment safety applies to the treasury too: credit the treasury's internal books from delivered_amount, never the Amount field, on incoming fee payments.

best_for.purpose: Auto-royalty on secondary NFT/asset sales to the studio (native TransferFee)
Percentage cut on fungible in-game token transfers (TransferRate)
Explicit per-sale fee payment to treasury with attribution tag

capabilities.name: Destination tags for custodial player sub-accounts
capabilities.summary: The standard way a custodial game backend credits the right player when many players share ONE on-ledger account. A single studio-controlled XRPL address pools all player funds; a 32-bit DestinationTag in each incoming Payment maps that deposit to a specific player's sub-account in the backend ledger. This is exactly how exchanges run 'hosted accounts'. SourceTag conversely lets the recipient know where to bounce a refund. Enable RequireDest on the pooled account so a deposit missing a tag is REJECTED rather than landing untagged and unattributable. The X-address format (X-prefixed) packs address + tag into one string so players cannot forget the tag — preferred UX for deposit addresses shown to players.
gotchas: A deposit WITHOUT the tag to a pooled account is unattributable — funds arrive but you can't tell whose they are. ALWAYS enable RequireDest on custodial pool accounts.

Destination tags are just integers with no on-ledger meaning — anyone can send any tag. Treat the tag as a routing hint, not authentication; the deposit's value is real but the claimed player must be validated against your own issued-tag registry.
Tags are 32-bit (0 to ~4.29B). For huge player bases, manage allocation/uniqueness carefully; don't reuse a tag for two players.
Surface deposit addresses to players as X-addresses (address+tag bundled) to eliminate the #1 cause of lost custodial deposits — the forgotten tag.

Custodial pooling means YOU hold the keys to everyone's funds — this is a regulatory and security posture (KYC/AML, hot-wallet risk), not just a technical choice. Non-custodial (player owns their own XRPL account) avoids the tag-routing problem entirely but shifts UX/recovery burden to the player.

best_for.purpose: Credit the correct player on a shared custodial deposit address
Hosted-account model for a game without per-player on-ledger accounts
Refund routing back to the originating player (source tag)

capabilities.name: Partial-payment-safe crediting (delivered_amount / DeliverMax)
capabilities.summary: The single most important backend-safety rule for any game that credits players from incoming XRPL payments. A Payment with the tfPartialPayment flag can deliver FAR LESS than its Amount field claims — the transaction still returns tesSUCCESS. If your backend reads Amount and credits the player that nominal value, an attacker sends a huge Amount with tfPartialPayment, delivers a few drops, and your game credits the full amount: direct theft. The fix: ALWAYS credit from the delivered_amount metadata field, never from Amount. In rippled API v2 the request-side field was renamed Amount -> DeliverMax precisely to stop this confusion; the actual-delivered figure remains delivered_amount in transaction metadata. This is non-negotiable for tournament prize-ins, marketplace settlement, deposits, and treasury fee accounting alike.
gotchas: Amount is a MAXIMUM/intended figure, not what arrived. Reading it to credit players is the classic XRPL exploit — multiple real exchanges have been hit, repeatedly.
A partial payment returns tesSUCCESS — success does NOT mean the full amount arrived. Never infer delivered value from the result code.
delivered_amount can be the string 'unavailable' for some very old (pre-2014) transactions — handle that case; for modern game flows it will be a real value.
API v2's DeliverMax rename helps but legacy code, old SDKs, and v1 responses still expose the misleading Amount — audit every integration path, not just the newest one.
Apply the same rule on EVERY incoming-value path: player deposits, P2P trade settlement, marketplace proceeds, and treasury fee receipts all credit from delivered_amount.
If you SEND payments and need a floor guarantee, set DeliverMin with tfPartialPayment so the transaction fails unless at least that much is delivered.

best_for.purpose: Safely crediting player deposits and prize-ins on a game backend
Reconciling marketplace/treasury receipts to actual value received
Guaranteeing a minimum delivered amount when sending (DeliverMin)

capabilities.name: Direct token Payment with trustline (player <-> game value transfer)
capabilities.summary: The base-layer flow underneath everything else: moving the studio's issued in-game token (an IOU on a trust line, or an MPT) between players and the game. A holder must establish a TrustLine to the issuer before they can receive that token; the Payment transaction then moves a token Amount {currency, issuer, value} from sender to recipient. This is the mainnet-available, no-amendment-needed primitive for routine rewards-in, purchases, and transfers when atomicity across multiple legs isn't required. MPTs (MPTokensV1, enabled on mainnet) offer a lighter-weight fungible-token option than classic trustline IOUs, with no per-holder reserve scaling the same way — attractive for games minting a points/currency token to many holders.
gotchas: Recipients CANNOT hold an IOU without a trust line to the issuer first (TrustSet). A reward Payment to a player with no trust line fails — onboarding must create the trust line before first payout.

Each trust line costs owner reserve on the holder's account; a token held by millions of players multiplies reserve burden. MPTs were designed to ease this — evaluate MPT vs trustline IOU before launch.
TransferRate (issuer-set) skims a fee on holder-to-holder token transfers — factor it into displayed prices so players aren't surprised by shortfalls.
Always credit recipients from delivered_amount, not Amount (see partial-payment-safe crediting) — this applies to token payments too.

Clawback (enabled on mainnet, default-vote No, opt-in per issuer) lets the issuer recover tokens for compliance — a power to wield carefully in a game economy; players may object to an issuer that can claw back their balance.

best_for.purpose: Routine in-game token rewards-in and player purchases
Simple player-to-player token transfer (non-atomic)
Minting a high-holder-count points/currency token (MPT)

capabilities.name: Deferred / installment payout via time-locked escrow (XRP & token)
capabilities.summary: Schedule future or vesting payouts to players without keeping a backend cron job in the trust path: create one or more EscrowCreate objects with FinishAfter timestamps so funds (XRP, in-game token, or MPT) become claimable on a schedule — a season-pass drip, a vesting team/creator allocation, or a 'locked until launch' pre-sale allotment. The ledger enforces the time lock; the player (or anyone) submits EscrowFinish once FinishAfter passes. CancelAfter provides a reclaim deadline so abandoned allotments return to the treasury. Post-XLS-85 these vesting schedules can be denominated in the studio's own token, not just XRP.
gotchas: Each escrow is a separate ledger object consuming owner reserve on the treasury — a fine-grained vesting drip (e.g. daily for a year) means hundreds of objects and reserve; coarser schedules are cheaper.
Token escrows MUST have an expiration (CancelAfter) and require the issuer to have enabled the token-escrow flag — a vesting schedule in a token whose issuer didn't opt in won't create.

Time-only escrows (no Condition) can be finished by ANYONE after FinishAfter, but funds go to the pre-set Destination — fine, but the player may need a nudge/automation to submit EscrowFinish; consider finishing on their behalf.
No Batch on mainnet means you can't create N installment escrows atomically — a partial failure mid-setup leaves an inconsistent vesting schedule; make setup idempotent and reconcile.
Time bounds use Ripple-epoch seconds — off-by-epoch errors are a classic bug; compute timestamps carefully.

best_for.purpose: Vesting / scheduled team or creator token allocations
Season-pass or pre-sale 'locked until date' player allotment
Instant, non-scheduled rewards

research.notes: 2026 depth synthesis for an in-game token economy. As of mid-2026 two production-grade fungible-token primitives co-exist on XRPL mainnet: trust-line IOUs (decade-old, bidirectional, rippling, currency-code identity) and Multi-Purpose Tokens (MPTokensV1 enabled 2025-10-01, rippled 2.3.0; unidirectional, integer-only, per-issuance 192-bit ID, on-chain config + 1024-byte metadata). For GAME CURRENCY the choice is doctrinal, not cosmetic. MPT wins for HARD currency: it has a native MaximumAmount supply cap (1..2^63-1) baked into the issuance ledger entry, configuration flags chosen once at MPTokenIssuanceCreate and then IMMUTABLE (CanTransfer/CanEscrow/CanClawback/CanLock/RequireAuth/CanTrade), AssetScale for decimals, and a single account can mint dozens of distinct currencies without one-account-per-currency contortions. IOU wins for SOFT currency where you want unlimited mint-on-demand (no cap field), post-hoc policy changes (set/clear flags any time), DEX/AMM liquidity TODAY (MPT DEX trading via XLS-82/MPTokensV2 is still in development, NOT mainnet in mid-2026), and mature wallet/explorer support. Supply control levers differ: MPT cap is enforced by the protocol (re-issue after burn allowed up to the cap); IOU has no cap so supply discipline is an off-ledger issuer policy. Economy-management (recall exploited gold, sanction a botter) uses Clawback (IOU Clawback enabled 2024-02-08; MPT CanClawback flag) plus Freeze tiers (IOU Individual/Global Freeze always available unless NoFreeze set; Deep Freeze via XLS-77 enabled 2025-05-05; MPT CanLock flag gives equivalent individual+global lock). Reserve math is the silent tax on multi-currency design: every token a player HOLDS (each IOU trust line OR each MPToken object) costs the holder 0.2 XRP owner reserve, so 'one token per faction/dungeon' designs scale linearly into real XRP the PLAYER must lock. Premium-vs-earned two-currency design is the sweet spot: premium hard currency as a capped, clawback-enabled, RequireAuth-gated MPT; earned soft currency as an uncapped IOU (or a second uncapped-by-policy MPT). Pin issuer config decisions in a design doc because MPT flags cannot be changed after mint.

capabilities.name: MPT as fixed-supply hard currency (MaximumAmount cap)
capabilities.summary: An MPToken issuance carries a protocol-enforced MaximumAmount (1 to 2^63-1 integer units), making it the natural primitive for a HARD in-game currency where total supply is a designed, auditable constant (premium gems, a deflationary trophy currency, a scarce governance token). The cap lives in the MPTokenIssuance ledger entry and the ledger refuses any mint that would push circulating supply past it. Because MPT uses fixed-precision integers with AssetScale for the decimal point, there is no rippling and no surprise inflation path. If holders burn tokens back to the issuer, the issuer may re-mint up to the cap, so the cap bounds MAX circulating, not lifetime mints.

capabilities.name: Clawback as an economy-recall lever (IOU + MPT)
capabilities.summary: Clawback lets the issuer forcibly recover issued tokens from a holder's balance — the single most important anti-exploit lever for a live game economy (recall duplicated gold from an exploited mint bug, drain a confirmed botter/RMT account, reverse a fraudulent transfer). For IOUs, the issuer enables it with the lsfAllowTrustLineClawback AccountSet flag BEFORE issuing, then sends a Clawback transaction. For MPTs, the issuer must set tfMPTCanClawback at issuance and then claw back from a holder's MPToken. Clawback never applies to native XRP.
capabilities.key_fields: IOU: AccountSet asfAllowTrustlineClawback (must be set before any tokens issued; one-way, cannot be disabled) then Clawback tx; MPT: tfMPTCanClawback(0x40) at MPTokenIssuanceCreate then Clawback tx referencing the holder + MPTokenIssuanceID; cannot claw back XRP
capabilities.gotchas: Must be opted in BEFORE issuance for both models — you cannot enable clawback on an IOU after any token is issued, and MPT flags are immutable, so a currency minted without the clawback flag is permanently un-recallable. This is a powerful, irreversible (for the holder) action: pair it with a named compensator/audit trail and clear ToS, since players experience a clawback as confiscation. Clawing back does not by itself stop the holder from re-acquiring the currency — combine with Freeze/Lock to fully sanction.

capabilities.name: Freeze tiers as sanction levers (Individual / Global / Deep Freeze)
capabilities.summary: For IOU game currencies the issuer has a graduated sanction ladder. Individual Freeze (tfSetFreeze on a trust line) stops a specific holder from sending the currency to anyone but the issuer and unfunds their offers, while they can still RECEIVE — good for a temporary penalty. Deep Freeze (XLS-77, enabled 2025-05-05) extends Individual Freeze so the holder also cannot RECEIVE the currency — a full quarantine of an abusive account. Global Freeze (lsfGlobalFreeze) halts the entire currency at once — the doomsday circuit-breaker for a compromised issuer or planned shutdown.

capabilities.name: Per-holder owner reserve as a multi-currency design budget
capabilities.summary: Every distinct token a PLAYER holds costs them owner reserve: each trust-line (RippleState) and each MPToken object is one ledger object at the current 0.2 XRP per-object reserve. A 'currency per faction / per dungeon / per season' design therefore charges the player real, locked XRP that scales linearly with the number of token types — the silent constraint that should bound multi-currency ambition. Design few, meaningful currencies (premium + earned, maybe one event currency) rather than a sprawling currency zoo, and account for who funds the reserve (player wallet vs studio-sponsored accounts).

capabilities.name: MPT transfer fee vs IOU TransferRate as a currency sink

For IOU, the issuer's TransferRate plays the same role on rippling transfers. A modest transfer fee on a tradeable earned currency taxes trading and sinks supply without a manual mint/burn loop.

research.notes: Wave-3 depth pass for a studio standing up tradeable liquidity for an in-game token (call it GOLD), assuming the Wave-1 DEX/AMM primitives are already known. The recommended pattern in mid-2026: issue GOLD as a normal issued currency, then bootstrap ONE shallow AMM pool as the price floor/always-on liquidity (GOLD/XRP for pure crypto liquidity, or GOLD/RLUSD when you want players to price the token in dollars), and let the native CLOB carry deeper player-to-player order flow on top — the two share liquidity automatically because OfferCreate and Payment route through whichever of {pool, order book, both} gives the best rate (Wave-1 covered that routing; here it matters because your single pool effectively backstops every player market). Bootstrapping mechanics that are easy to get wrong: AMMCreate must fund BOTH assets and seeds the price; it costs a special one-time creation fee (the owner-reserve-scaled AMMCreate fee, historically ~0.2 XRP-class, not the base tx fee) and there can be only ONE AMM per asset pair, so the studio's first AMMCreate is the canonical GOLD/XRP venue forever. To deepen a pool the treasury already seeded, use AMMDeposit single-asset (tfSingleAsset / tfLimitLPToken) so you can add GOLD-only or XRP-only without pre-balancing — but single-asset deposits pay the pool's trading fee (priced as if you traded half then did a two-asset deposit), so large single-sided injections suffer slippage; for the very first deposit into an emptied pool use tfTwoAssetIfEmpty to reset the ratio without a fee. The treasury's LPToken is itself a tradeable XRPL token and the studio's liquidity receipt — it is how you withdraw, it appreciates from accrued fees, it can be escrowed/clawed/used as collateral, and (gotcha) it carries the standard issued-token trustline reserve. Revenue: the AMM trading fee (0%–1%, set/changed via AMMVote weighted by LPToken share, top-8 voters) accrues pro-rata to LPs — so a treasury that holds most LPTokens earns most of the swap fees on its own token; AMMBid lets the treasury (or an arbitrage bot) pay LPTokens for a 24h discounted-fee auction slot, and outbidding refunds the prior holder pro-rata by time elapsed. Price discovery for a thin game token is the real risk: a single shallow pool is trivially manipulable, so do NOT wire game logic (shop prices, reward payouts, sink costs) directly to instantaneous pool spot price. Use XLS-47 Price Oracle (OracleSet/OracleDelete + get_aggregate_price, live since rippled 2.2.0) to publish/consume a smoothed reference price with trimmed-mean + age checks, and treat the AMM as the trade venue, not the truth source. AMM-vs-CLOB for a game economy: AMM = zero-maintenance always-on liquidity + fee revenue + good for the long tail of casual swaps; CLOB = no slippage at the quote, limit orders, market-maker depth, and the place power-users and guild treasuries will actually trade size — ship the AMM as the floor and let the CLOB form on top. For regulated / real-money or jurisdiction-gated economies, XLS-81 Permissioned DEX (enabled 2026-02-18) on top of XLS-80 Permissioned Domains (enabled 2026-02-04) lets you require a credential (KYC/region/age) to place or take GOLD offers via the offer's DomainID, with Hybrid offers checking the private pool first then falling back to the open DEX. All amendment dates and flag semantics below were web-verified against xrpl.org and XRPLF/XRPL-Standards in June 2026.

capabilities.name: AMMCreate (stand up the canonical game-token pool)
capabilities.summary: The one-time transaction that mints the studio's GOLD/XRP (or GOLD/RLUSD) automated market maker. It creates the AMM AccountRoot + AMM ledger object, funds it with the two assets you supply (which seeds the starting price = ratio of the two amounts), sets the initial trading fee, and issues the first LPTokens to the creator. There can be exactly one AMM per asset pair on the whole ledger, so the studio's first AMMCreate for GOLD/XRP is the canonical, permanent venue — pick the seed amounts and the asset pairing deliberately because the starting price and fee are yours to set here.

key_fields.Amount / Amount2: the two assets to deposit (e.g. GOLD issued amount + XRP drops); their ratio sets the opening price
key_fields.special_fee: AMMCreate charges a one-time owner-reserve-scaled creation fee (historically ~0.2 XRP class), NOT just the base tx fee — budget for it
key_fields.uniqueness: only ONE AMM may exist per asset pair ledger-wide
key_fields.result: creates AMM object + special AccountRoot (lsfAMMNode), issues LPTokens to creator

capabilities.gotchas: Seeding at a wrong ratio = wrong opening price that arbitrageurs will instantly drain value from; compute the seed amounts against your intended GOLD price. The creation fee is materially larger than a normal transaction and is non-refundable. You cannot create a second pool for the same pair to 'fix' a mistake — you'd have to AMMWithdraw fully, AMMDelete, and re-create. Both assets must already be held/trustlined by the creating account before AMMCreate.

capabilities.name: LPToken as treasury liquidity receipt & yield instrument
capabilities.summary: The pool-share token the AMM issues to liquidity providers. For the studio it is the treasury's claim on the GOLD pool: holding it is how you withdraw, it grows in redemption value as swap fees accrue to the pool, and because it is a fully ordinary XRPL issued token it can itself be traded, escrowed, sent in payments, clawed back (if the underlying supports it), or pledged. Your LPToken share also determines your AMMVote weight (fee governance) and what you can bid on the AMMBid auction slot. Tracking the treasury's LPToken balance vs. total LPTokens outstanding tells you what fraction of pool fees and pool value the studio owns.

key_fields.value: redeemable for a pro-rata slice of both pool assets at withdrawal time
key_fields.yield: grows as AMM trading fees accrue to the pool (no separate claim tx needed)

key_fields.fungibility: a normal issued token — tradeable, payable, escrowable; needs a trustline + reserve

capabilities.gotchas: Holding LPTokens consumes a trustline owner reserve like any issued asset. Impermanent loss applies: if GOLD's price diverges hard from the seed ratio the LPToken's redemption value can be worth less than just holding the two assets — for a volatile freshly-launched game token this can be significant. The LPToken currency code is auto-derived from the pool, not human-readable. Selling/transferring LPTokens transfers the underlying liquidity claim — don't treat them as cosmetic.

capabilities.name: AMMVote — set/govern the swap fee as studio revenue
capabilities.summary: The mechanism that sets the GOLD pool's 0%-1% trading fee, which is the studio's direct on-chain revenue line from player swaps: fees accrue to the pool and therefore to LPToken holders pro-rata, so a treasury that holds most LPTokens earns most of the fees on its own token. Fee changes are governed by weighted voting — each LP's vote is weighted by LPTokens held, the pool recomputes its fee as the LPToken-weighted average of the latest votes, and only the top 8 voters (by LPTokens) are counted. While the treasury dominates the pool it effectively sets the fee unilaterally.

key_fields.weighting: vote weight = voter's LPToken balance; result = weighted average of latest votes
key_fields.top_8: at most 8 LPs' votes are counted — top 8 by LPTokens held
key_fields.revenue_model: fees accrue to the pool -> raise LPToken redemption value -> treasury earns its share

capabilities.gotchas: Fee is capped at 1% — it is a liquidity-incentive knob, not a primary monetization channel; over-fee and players route around your pool via the CLOB. If outside LPs accumulate enough LPTokens they can outvote the treasury (top-8 weighted), so monitor the cap table. Setting fee to 0 removes your revenue but maximizes routing through your pool — a real tradeoff for launch-phase liquidity bootstrapping.

best_for.purpose: Turn player swap volume into studio fee revenue
Tune fee to balance liquidity attraction vs. revenue
Decentralized fee governance among multiple LPs

capabilities.name: AMMBid — auction slot for discounted-fee market making
capabilities.summary: Pay LPTokens to claim a 24-hour 'auction slot' that gives the holder a discounted (down to zero) trading fee on the pool. For a game economy this is the studio's (or a contracted bot's) lever to run arbitrage and price-keeping against the GOLD pool cheaply — keep the pool's spot near the oracle reference without paying the full swap fee each round-trip. The minimum bid for an empty/expired slot is (total LPTokens outstanding x trading fee) / 25; outbidding an active holder costs at least the min plus up to 105% of the current holder's price, and refunds the displaced holder pro-rata by time remaining.

key_fields.AuthAccounts: up to 4 extra accounts that also get the discount (e.g. studio MM bots)
key_fields.duration: slot lasts 24 hours, discounted fee for the holder
key_fields.outbid_refund: displaced holder refunded pro-rata to time elapsed in the 24h window

capabilities.gotchas: The bid is burned LPTokens (paid back to the pool, benefiting all LPs incl. the studio) — net cost to a dominant treasury is small, but for a minority holder it is real spend. Only worthwhile if there is enough swap volume that the fee discount + arbitrage edge exceeds the bid. The slot discount applies only to the holder + its AuthAccounts, so name your MM bot accounts. Peripheral for a pure casual game economy; matters once volume and arbitrage are real.

capabilities.name: Native CLOB order book for player-to-player markets (OfferCreate)
capabilities.summary: The genesis-era central limit order book where players post limit orders to buy/sell GOLD against XRP, RLUSD, or each other's tokens via OfferCreate (cancel via OfferCancel). For a game economy this is where real depth and price discovery happen on top of the AMM floor: power-users, guild treasuries, and traders post resting limit orders the AMM can't replicate (no slippage at the quoted price, exact-price fills), and the studio gets a fully on-chain, no-server player marketplace for free. Crucially, OfferCreate already consults the GOLD AMM pool and routes through pool/book/both for the best rate, so the single studio pool backstops every order-book price.

capabilities.name: Auto-bridging for cross-currency player trades
capabilities.summary: When a player trades two non-XRP currencies — e.g. GOLD for another game's token, or GOLD for RLUSD when no direct GOLD/RLUSD book exists — the ledger automatically synthesizes a route through XRP (GOLD->XRP->target) whenever that is cheaper than the direct book, deepening effective liquidity for thin pairs. For a game economy this means the studio only needs to seed strong GOLD/XRP liquidity (one pool + one book) and players can still trade GOLD against many currencies at a good rate, because XRP acts as the universal bridge. It happens automatically on any OfferCreate and on cross-currency Payments via the Flow pathfinding engine — no special transaction.

key_fields.mechanism: synthetic GOLD->XRP->target route auto-considered alongside the direct book
key_fields.trigger: automatic on OfferCreate and cross-currency Payment; chosen only if cheaper
key_fields.implication: seed GOLD/XRP deeply and many GOLD/* pairs become tradeable
key_fields.engine: Flow pathfinding combines bridged + direct offers + AMM for best total rate

capabilities.gotchas: Auto-bridging only kicks in through XRP — a GOLD/RLUSD trade benefits only if there is GOLD/XRP AND XRP/RLUSD liquidity. It is not a substitute for seeding the pairs your players actually use most. Bridged routes touch more order books, so a single trade can move several pools/books at once — model this when reasoning about price impact and oracle inputs. Pathfinding suggestions from a server are advisory; the on-ledger Flow engine recomputes the actual best path at execution.

capabilities.name: Price Oracle (XLS-47) for game-token price discovery
capabilities.summary: Native on-ledger price oracles (introduced in rippled 2.2.0): OracleSet creates/updates a PriceOracle ledger entry holding signed price-pair data, OracleDelete removes it, and the get_aggregate_price API returns an aggregated (mean / median / trimmed-mean) price across multiple oracle instances with a standard deviation. For a thin game token this is the safe way to do price discovery: rather than wiring shop prices, reward payouts, or sink costs to the instantaneous AMM spot (trivially manipulable in a shallow pool), publish/consume a smoothed, multi-source, age-checked reference price. The same oracle infrastructure feeds AMM-adjacent DeFi (lending, vaults) so it is the canonical truth source while the AMM/CLOB remain the trade venues.

key_fields.OracleSet: creates/updates a PriceOracle entry with PriceDataSeries (base/quote, asset price, scale)
key_fields.get_aggregate_price: API: aggregated mean/median/trimmed-mean across oracles + std dev + timestamps
key_fields.freshness: each price datum carries a timestamp — consumers must enforce max age

capabilities.gotchas: An oracle is only as honest as its publishers — for a game token YOU are likely the publisher, so a compromised oracle key lets an attacker set any 'price'; protect oracle-signing keys and consider multiple independent feeds + trimmed-mean to resist a single bad source. Always enforce a max-age / staleness check; a frozen oracle returning a stale price is a classic exploit vector. The oracle does not auto-derive price from your AMM — you must publish to it (e.g. a keeper that reads pool TWAP, smooths it, and OracleSets). Don't confuse the oracle (truth) with the AMM (venue).

best_for.purpose: Smoothed, manipulation-resistant reference price for game logic
Decouple shop/reward/sink pricing from manipulable spot price

capabilities.name: AMM-vs-CLOB choice for a game economy (architecture pattern)
capabilities.summary: The architectural decision a studio actually has to make: AMM, CLOB, or both. Because XRPL routes a single offer/payment through pool + book + both for the best rate, the answer for a game economy is almost always BOTH, with a deliberate division of labor. Seed ONE AMM pool (GOLD/XRP or GOLD/RLUSD) as the always-on liquidity floor and fee-revenue engine — it needs zero maintenance, guarantees a tradeable price from day one, and serves the long tail of casual swaps. Let the CLOB form on top for depth: limit orders, no slippage at the quote, and the venue where guilds/power-users/MM bots trade size. Use the oracle as the price truth, the AMM as the floor, the CLOB as the depth, auto-bridging as the connectivity, and Permissioned DEX if access must be gated.

key_fields.AMM_strengths: always-on, zero-maintenance, fee revenue, no order management, good for casual long-tail
key_fields.AMM_weaknesses: slippage in shallow pools, impermanent loss for the LP, manipulable spot for thin tokens
key_fields.CLOB_strengths: no slippage at quote, limit orders, real depth, where size trades, no IL
key_fields.CLOB_weaknesses: needs active makers (no built-in fee incentive), thin at launch, per-order reserve
key_fields.recommended: ship AMM floor + let CLOB form on top; they share liquidity automatically

capabilities.gotchas: Do NOT pick one and ignore the other thinking you must — the ledger already unifies them, so 'AMM-only' just means a worse experience for size traders and 'CLOB-only' means no day-one liquidity. Don't over-fund the AMM for a volatile launch token (impermanent loss can burn the treasury); start with a modest pool as the floor and let the CLOB carry growth. Never make in-game economy logic depend on AMM spot — that is the oracle's job (see price-oracle-xls47).

capabilities.name: Permissioned DEX (XLS-81) for regulated game economies

research.notes: Wave-3 DEPTH synthesis (verified mid-2026) of how to BUILD a game token economy on XRPL primitives. The load-bearing currency check this lane depends on resolved with a surprise: the mass-payout primitive everyone designs around -- Batch (XLS-56) -- is NOT available. A critical signature-validation flaw (unauthorized inner-transaction execution) was disclosed 2026-02-19 (Keshkamat + Cantina AI/Apex) and rippled 3.1.1 (2026-02-23) explicitly marked the original Batch amendment AND fixBatchInnerSigs as UNSUPPORTED, blocking validator votes on every production network. The successor BatchV1_1 is implemented but still UNDER REVIEW with NO scheduled date as of June 2026. Net consequence for builders: do NOT design your reward distribution around atomic batch payouts in 2026 -- you must loop individual Payment transactions (sequence-managed, server-side) for quest rewards and drops, and treat atomic multi-recipient payout as a roadmap item, not a current capability. The rest of the economy stack is in much better shape and is the real story of this lane: (1) MPT (MPTokensV1, mainnet 2025-10-01) is the right substrate for SOFT/EARNED currency -- it needs NO trust line (zero per-holder reserve to onboard a player into the currency), supports a native on-ledger transfer fee of 0-50% in 0.0001% steps PAID BY BURNING the tokens (a sink you get for free), a hard MaximumAmount supply cap up to 2^63-1, an AssetScale for decimals, 1024 bytes of on-chain metadata, and immutable-at-issuance compliance flags (CanTransfer, CanClawback, CanLock, RequireAuth, CanEscrow). (2) Classic IOU/trust-line tokens remain the right substrate for a HARD/PREMIUM currency that must trade on the native DEX/AMM -- but every holder costs a 0.2 XRP trust-line reserve and MPT's CanTrade flag is reserved/not-yet-implemented, so MPTs cannot list on the DEX in 2026. (3) The IOU TransferRate sink (0-100%, encoded as billionths, e.g. 1005000000 = 0.5%) is ALSO a burn -- fee tokens are destroyed, NOT credited to the issuer -- and is EXEMPT on transfers to/from the issuer, which is exactly the mint/redeem doorway you want. (4) XLS-85 Token Escrow (mainnet 2026-02-12) finally extends native time-lock/conditional escrow to IOUs and MPTs, making vesting and structured treasury payouts possible WITHOUT a smart contract. (5) XRP itself is the gas/reserve layer: every tx burns ~10 drops (destroyed, not paid to validators), accounts cost 1 XRP base reserve + 0.2 XRP per owned object. CURRENCY MAPPING VERDICT: soft/earned currency -> MPT (cheap onboarding, native burn sink, supply cap, clawback for anti-RMT); hard/premium currency -> IOU if it must hit the DEX/AMM, otherwise MPT; XRP -> reserve/gas + neutral settlement rail, never the in-game soft currency. ON-CHAIN vs OFF-CHAIN VERDICT: keep the high-frequency game loop, inventory bookkeeping, and most balances OFF-chain in your authoritative server; put on-chain ONLY the trust anchors -- final ownership of tradeable items (NFTs), withdrawable currency balances at cash-out boundaries, treasury movements, and marketplace settlement -- because XRPL is fast and cheap but still ledger-paced (~3-4s) and every on-chain object carries a reserve. ANTI-RMT / ANTI-INFLATION: native levers are clawback (MPT/IOU), trust-line freeze, RequireAuth allow-listing of who may hold the currency, the two transfer-fee burns above as friction-on-resale, hard supply caps, and escrow-gated emission -- combined, these let a studio retain the compliance hooks (recover stolen/laundered balances, throttle secondary trade) that pure-decentralization designs lack. The honest gap: no atomic batch payout (Batch disabled), no MPT-on-DEX yet (CanTrade unimplemented), and no native smart-contract sink logic -- routing of marketplace/crafting fees to a treasury or burn address is done by your server constructing ordinary Payment txs, not by on-chain hooks.

capabilities.name: Dual-currency mapping: MPT (soft/earned) vs IOU (hard/tradeable) vs XRP (gas/settlement)
capabilities.summary: The foundational economy-design decision: which XRPL primitive backs which currency. Map SOFT/EARNED currency (gold, quest points -- the spammy, high-volume, sink-heavy one) to a Multi-Purpose Token, because MPTs need NO trust line so onboarding a player costs zero per-holder reserve, carry a native burn-based transfer fee as a free sink, and enforce a hard supply cap. Map HARD/PREMIUM currency (the one players buy with real money and may trade) to a classic IOU trust-line token ONLY if it must live on the native DEX/AMM, since MPTs cannot trade on the DEX in 2026; otherwise a second MPT issuance is fine. Keep XRP out of the in-game currency role entirely -- it is the reserve/gas substrate and a neutral settlement/cash-out rail, not the gold pile.
capabilities.key_fields: MPT: no trust line, MaximumAmount cap, transfer fee 0-50% burned, AssetScale for decimals, clawback/freeze/RequireAuth flags. IOU: requires 0.2 XRP trust-line reserve per holder, TransferRate 0-100% burned, DEX/AMM-tradeable. XRP: 1 XRP account reserve + 0.2 XRP per object, ~10 drop tx burn. Use separate issuing accounts per currency to isolate transfer-fee policy (one TransferRate applies to ALL IOUs from one issuer).
capabilities.gotchas: Do NOT make the soft currency an IOU -- you would pay 0.2 XRP reserve for every player to hold gold, which does not scale to a free-to-play install base. Do NOT assume an MPT can be traded on the XRPL DEX/AMM in 2026: the CanTrade flag exists in the spec but is reserved/NOT IMPLEMENTED, so the tradeable premium currency must be an IOU today. A single issuing account applies ONE TransferRate to every token it issues, so if soft and hard currency need different sinks they need different issuers.

capabilities.name: MPT as soft-currency substrate (MPTokensV1)
capabilities.summary: The concrete recipe for an earned in-game currency on XRPL. MPTokensV1 went live on mainnet 2025-10-01. Issue one MPT via MPTokenIssuanceCreate with a MaximumAmount cap (your designed monetary base), an AssetScale (decimal precision), 1024 bytes of compressed-JSON on-chain metadata (ticker/name/icon), and the compliance flags you need locked at issuance (CanTransfer to allow P2P, CanClawback for recovery, CanLock for freeze, RequireAuth for allow-listing, CanEscrow for vesting). Players hold it with ZERO trust-line reserve, which is the property that makes it viable for a mass free-to-play audience. The native transfer fee is your built-in resale sink.

Holders use MPTokenAuthorize (no XRP reserve cost to opt in). Flags except lsfMPTLocked are IMMUTABLE after creation.
capabilities.gotchas: Almost all issuance flags are SET ONCE AND PERMANENT -- you cannot add CanClawback or CanTransfer later, so decide your anti-RMT/compliance posture before minting. CanTrade is in the spec but NOT IMPLEMENTED, so an MPT cannot be listed on the XRPL DEX/AMM in 2026 (use an IOU for any DEX-traded currency). MaximumAmount is a hard ceiling -- if you under-size it you cannot raise it, so model your faucet/sink balance and lifetime emission before setting it.

capabilities.name: Native transfer-fee burn as a currency sink (MPT TransferFee & IOU TransferRate)
capabilities.summary: XRPL gives you a deflationary sink for free: a configurable percentage of every secondary transfer is DESTROYED, not pocketed by anyone. For IOUs set TransferRate (0-100%, encoded as billionths -- 1005000000 = 0.5%); the sender is debited the extra, the recipient gets the intended amount, and the fee tokens are burned. For MPTs set TransferFee (0-50% in 0.0001% steps) which is likewise paid by burning. Crucially the fee is EXEMPT on transfers directly to/from the issuing account, so minting (faucet) and redeeming (cash-out doorway) are friction-free while every player-to-player trade leaks supply. This is the canonical anti-inflation lever and a passive anti-RMT friction in one primitive.
capabilities.key_fields: IOU: TransferRate integer where 1000000000 = 0% and 2000000000 = 100%, rounded to nearest 0.0000001%, applies to ALL tokens from that issuer. MPT: TransferFee 0-50.000% in 0.0001% increments, set once at issuance. Both BURN the fee (removed from ledger, not credited to issuer). Both EXEMPT when one leg is the issuer.
capabilities.gotchas: The fee is a BURN, not revenue -- if you want marketplace fees to flow to the studio treasury you must route a separate Payment, not rely on TransferRate (see the marketplace-fee-routing pattern). One IOU issuer = one TransferRate for every token it issues; segregate currencies across issuers if they need different rates. Because the issuer leg is exempt, routing every trade through the issuer (a hub-and-spoke pattern) accidentally waives the sink -- keep player-to-player transfers direct if you want the burn to apply.

best_for.purpose: Building a passive deflationary sink that fights long-run currency inflation
Adding resale friction that mildly discourages real-money trading

capabilities.name: Reward distribution at scale (and the Batch XLS-56 gap)
capabilities.summary: The hardest current reality of XRPL game economics: there is NO atomic mass-payout primitive on mainnet in 2026. Batch (XLS-56) -- the intended way to group many inner Payments into one atomic transaction -- was found to have a critical signature-validation flaw (an attacker could execute inner transactions on arbitrary victim accounts without their keys), disclosed 2026-02-19, and rippled 3.1.1 (2026-02-23) marked both Batch and fixBatchInnerSigs UNSUPPORTED so validators cannot enable them. The successor BatchV1_1 is implemented but UNDER REVIEW with no date. Until then, distribute quest rewards and drops by looping INDIVIDUAL Payment transactions from your faucet/issuer account: a server-side sender that manages the account Sequence (or uses Tickets to parallelize), submits N payments, and reconciles results. Each payment is exempt from the transfer fee if it comes from the issuer.
capabilities.key_fields: Current path: N x Payment txs from one funded sender; manage Sequence numbers strictly in order OR pre-allocate Tickets (TicketCreate) to submit out-of-order/in-parallel. Each tx burns ~10 drops of XRP. Issuer-leg payments are transfer-fee-exempt (full reward delivered). Failed Batch hash/details in XLS-0056-batch repo; BatchV1_1 removes the early-exit in signer validation. NO atomic all-or-nothing semantics available in 2026.
capabilities.gotchas: Do NOT architect your payout system assuming Batch exists -- it is disabled and may stay so for an unknown period. Looping Payments is NOT atomic: partial failure is possible, so your server must track which recipients succeeded and retry idempotently. Sequence-number contention is the classic footgun for high-throughput payout; use Tickets to avoid serializing every payout behind one Sequence. Throughput is also ledger-paced (~3-4s/ledger, finite tx/ledger), so very large drops are batched over time off-chain, not instant.

best_for.purpose: Designing a quest-reward / airdrop payout pipeline that works on mainnet TODAY
Knowing what to wait for (BatchV1_1) before relying on atomic multi-recipient payouts

capabilities.name: Treasury management via Token Escrow (XLS-85) for vesting & structured payouts
capabilities.summary: Studio treasury and emission control without a smart contract. XLS-85 Token Escrow went live on mainnet 2026-02-12, extending native time-locked / conditional escrow -- previously XRP-only -- to IOU trust-line tokens AND MPTs. For a game economy this gives you: vesting schedules for team/partner currency allocations, escrow-gated emission (lock the season's reward pool and release it on a finish-after time so the faucet cannot over-emit), and structured/scheduled treasury payouts -- all enforced by the ledger. A finish-after-only escrow sits Held until its time passes, then becomes Ready and anyone can EscrowFinish it.
capabilities.key_fields: EscrowCreate with Amount as an IOU or MPT (post-XLS-85), FinishAfter (time-based release), optional Condition (crypto-condition). Each escrowed object costs 0.2 XRP owner reserve while active. Held -> Ready (after FinishAfter) -> finished via EscrowFinish; CancelAfter returns funds. Supports stablecoins (e.g. RLUSD) and any on-ledger token.
capabilities.gotchas: Each active escrow consumes a 0.2 XRP owner reserve, so escrow is for treasury-scale movements (a few large locks), NOT for per-player micro-vesting (thousands of escrows = thousands of reserves). Escrow is not a general programmable vault -- it is time/condition release only; complex emission curves still need your server to create successive escrows. Verify the token issuer hasn't frozen/clawed the asset, which can interact with escrowed balances.

capabilities.name: Faucet implementation (quest rewards & drops via issuer Payments)
capabilities.summary: How currency ENTERS the economy. The faucet is your authoritative game server constructing Payment transactions FROM the issuing account TO the player, triggered by validated game events (quest completion, monster drop, daily login). Because payments from the issuer are exempt from the transfer fee, the player receives the full designed reward. For MPT soft currency the player needs only a prior MPTokenAuthorize (no reserve); for IOU currency the player must hold a trust line first. The faucet is the single throttle point for emission -- rate, caps, and anti-abuse all live in your server, with the ledger as the durable settlement record.
capabilities.key_fields: Payment tx: Account=issuer, Destination=player, Amount=MPT or IOU. Issuer-leg = transfer-fee-exempt. Player prerequisite: MPTokenAuthorize (MPT, no reserve) or TrustSet (IOU, 0.2 XRP reserve). Emission control = server logic (per-event reward tables, daily caps, supply-cap awareness vs MaximumAmount). Pair with escrow (XLS-85) to pre-commit a bounded season pool.
capabilities.gotchas: All emission policy is OFF-chain in your server -- the ledger will happily mint up to MaximumAmount, so anti-inflation discipline is YOUR responsibility, not the protocol's. A compromised issuer key = unbounded mint; protect it with multisign and keep the bulk of treasury in a separate cold account. No atomic batch means high-volume drop events are a managed Payment loop (Tickets for parallelism), not one transaction.

best_for.purpose: Wiring validated game events to on-ledger currency issuance
Centralizing emission throttle and anti-abuse at the faucet boundary

capabilities.name: Sink implementation (crafting costs, fee burns, redemption to issuer)
capabilities.summary: How currency LEAVES the economy -- the half most studios under-build. Three on-ledger sink mechanics: (1) REDEEM-TO-ISSUER: a Payment from player back to the issuing account effectively removes the tokens from circulation (the issuer's own balance is not a circulating supply); this is the cleanest crafting/shop sink -- player pays crafting cost to the issuer and the currency is retired. (2) NATIVE TRANSFER-FEE BURN on every secondary trade (MPT TransferFee / IOU TransferRate), a passive always-on sink. (3) XRP GAS BURN: every transaction destroys ~10 drops of XRP, a tiny structural sink on activity. There is NO on-chain hook to auto-burn on a game event, so crafting/shop sinks are your server sending the player's spend back to the issuer (or to a no-key burn/black-hole address).
capabilities.key_fields: Redeem sink: Payment Account=player -> Destination=issuer (tokens retired from circulation; transfer-fee-exempt on the issuer leg). Passive sink: MPT TransferFee / IOU TransferRate burn on P2P trades. Structural sink: ~10 drops XRP burned per tx. True burn address: a black-holed account (master key disabled, no regular key) for irrevocable removal. Sink magnitude is tuned in server-side cost tables, not on-chain.
capabilities.gotchas: Sending currency to the ISSUER reduces circulating supply but the issuer can re-emit it (it is not destroyed); for irreversible burn use a provably-unspendable black-holed address or, for MPT/IOU, rely on the transfer-fee burn which is true destruction. Don't conflate the two when modeling supply. As with faucets there is NO on-chain trigger -- the protocol won't burn on 'crafted an item'; your server must construct the sink Payment. Balance faucet emission against sink drainage explicitly (the faucet-and-sink discipline) or the soft currency inflates regardless of supply cap.

Stacking passive (transfer-fee) and active (redemption) sinks against inflation

capabilities.name: Anti-RMT & compliance levers (clawback, freeze, RequireAuth allow-listing)
capabilities.summary: Native issuer controls that let a studio retain a compliance grip the pure-decentralization crowd gives up -- essential for fighting real-money-trading, laundering, and stolen-balance abuse. Three levers, all set/used by the issuer: (1) CLAWBACK -- if the MPT was issued with CanClawback (or the IOU issuer enabled Clawback), the issuer can forcibly recover tokens from a holder via a Clawback transaction (recover stolen/fraudulent balances, reverse exploited gains). (2) FREEZE -- both issuer and holder can freeze a trust line; the issuer freeze (and MPT CanLock) immobilizes a suspect balance pending investigation. (3) REQUIREAUTH allow-listing -- with RequireAuth the issuer must explicitly authorize each holder before they can receive the currency, gating WHO is allowed into the economy at all. Layer these with the transfer-fee resale friction for a graduated anti-RMT posture.
capabilities.key_fields: Clawback: requires tfMPTCanClawback (MPT) / AllowTrustLineClawback (IOU) set at config time; executed via Clawback tx by the issuer. Freeze: issuer sets lsfGlobalFreeze or per-line freeze; MPT lsfMPTLocked toggled via MPTokenIssuanceSet. RequireAuth: issuer flag; holders need explicit authorization (TrustSet authorize / MPTokenAuthorize approval) before holding. All are issuer-only powers -- design them in BEFORE minting (most flags are immutable post-issuance).
capabilities.gotchas: Clawback and most compliance flags are IMMUTABLE after issuance -- you cannot retrofit CanClawback onto an existing MPT, so enable it at mint even if you hope never to use it. These powers undercut the 'players truly own it' promise; communicate the trust model honestly. RequireAuth makes onboarding heavier (an extra authorization step / server approval per player). Freeze/clawback are blunt -- pair with off-chain detection so you act on evidence, not vibes. None of these STOP RMT outright; they raise cost and enable post-hoc recovery.

best_for.purpose: Retaining recovery/compliance hooks against RMT, theft, and laundering

capabilities.name: On-chain vs off-chain split (the load-bearing economy decision)
capabilities.summary: The single decision that most shapes a hybrid game economy: what lives on the ledger vs in your authoritative server. The verified-pattern answer for a fast-but-ledger-paced chain like XRPL: keep the high-frequency game loop, full inventory, and most in-game balances OFF-chain (your server is the system of record for play); put ON-chain ONLY the trust anchors where decentralized ownership or external trade matters -- final ownership of tradeable items (NFTs), the withdrawable slice of currency at cash-out/deposit boundaries, treasury movements, and marketplace SETTLEMENT. This is the industry hybrid consensus: classical/off-chain for speed-critical play, on-chain for economics that must be provable and externally tradeable. It also contains RMT and regulatory surface, because most of the economy never touches a wallet.
capabilities.key_fields: Off-chain (server-authoritative): real-time combat, full inventory, soft-currency working balances, matchmaking, anti-cheat. On-chain (trust anchor): NFT item ownership for tradeable gear, currency balances at the deposit/withdraw boundary, marketplace settlement, treasury/escrow. Bridge = your server signs/submits XRPL txs at the boundary. Cost forcing function: every on-chain object carries an XRP reserve (1 base + 0.2/object) and ledger pace ~3-4s, so on-chain state is deliberately scarce.
capabilities.gotchas: Putting per-tick game state on-chain is the classic mistake -- reserves and ledger latency make it infeasible at game scale; XRPL is fast for a blockchain but not a game tickrate. The off-chain ledger is centralized -- be explicit about which balances are 'real' (on-chain, withdrawable) vs 'soft' (server-side, revocable). The boundary (deposit/withdraw) is the security-critical surface: it is where exploits convert game value to real value, so it gets the heaviest verification, rate-limits, and anti-RMT levers.

capabilities.name: Premium-currency liquidity via the native DEX & AMM (XLS-30)
capabilities.summary: If your HARD/PREMIUM currency must be exchangeable for XRP or stablecoins (player cash-out, real price discovery), back it with an IOU and use the native on-ledger DEX plus the AMM (XLS-30, mainnet since March 2024). The studio can seed an AMM pool (premium-token / XRP) to bootstrap liquidity so players can swap in/out without an external exchange. The AMM coexists with the order-book DEX and auto-routes for best price. This is what makes a premium currency a real, priced asset rather than a closed server credit -- but it also opens the cash-out boundary, so it is the riskiest piece for RMT and regulation and rates only 'useful' for most game designs (many should NOT make their currency freely tradeable).
capabilities.key_fields: AMM (XLS-30): constant-product pool per asset pair, trading fee voted by top-8 LPs, max 1% cap; AMMCreate/AMMDeposit/AMMWithdraw/AMMVote/AMMBid txs. Requires IOU (MPT CanTrade is NOT implemented, so MPTs can't pool/trade in 2026). Draft 'AMM Swappable Curves' (filed May 2026, NOT enabled) would add concentrated-liquidity and StableSwap curves. Native order-book DEX available alongside AMM.
capabilities.gotchas: MPTs CANNOT be on the DEX/AMM today -- this pattern is IOU-only, which forces a 0.2 XRP trust-line reserve per holder of the premium currency. Listing a currency for free trade is a deliberate RMT/regulatory choice: many games should keep premium currency NON-tradeable (server credit) and only let players cash OUT through a controlled boundary, not run a free market. AMM impermanent loss applies to studio-seeded liquidity. The richer curve types (StableSwap/concentrated) are draft-only as of mid-2026.

best_for.purpose: Giving a tradeable premium currency real liquidity and price discovery
Seeding a studio AMM pool to bootstrap a market for the hard currency

capabilities.name: Marketplace-fee routing to studio treasury
capabilities.summary: How the studio actually EARNS from secondary trade -- distinct from the transfer-fee BURN. The native transfer fee destroys tokens; it does NOT pay the studio. To route marketplace/crafting fees to a treasury you have two options: (1) for NFT item sales, set the NFT TransferFee at mint so the issuer/minter automatically receives a cut of every secondary sale brokered on-ledger; (2) for currency-denominated marketplace fees, your server constructs the trade as split Payments (buyer -> seller for the item price, buyer -> treasury for the fee) or brokers it so the treasury account receives its share. There is no on-chain hook to auto-skim a percentage of an arbitrary token Payment, so currency-fee routing is a server-built composite, not a protocol feature.
capabilities.key_fields: NFT royalty: NFTokenMint TransferFee field -> issuer/minter receives a percentage of brokered secondary sales automatically (this DOES accrue to the issuer, unlike fungible-token transfer fees which burn). Currency-fee routing: server splits into buyer->seller + buyer->treasury Payments, or uses brokered NFTokenAcceptOffer where the broker collects the spread. Treasury = a dedicated studio account (ideally multisign + separate from the live issuer hot key).
capabilities.gotchas: Do NOT expect the fungible TransferRate/TransferFee to fund the treasury -- those BURN. Studio revenue from currency trades must be an explicit treasury-bound Payment your server adds. NFT TransferFee only applies to sales brokered through the on-ledger NFT offer system; off-ledger or peer transfers can bypass it. With Batch disabled you cannot atomically bundle the item-transfer and the fee-payment, so server-side reconciliation must handle partial failure.

research.notes: DEPTH synthesis (mid-2026) on connecting a game economy to real value, built on but NOT repeating Wave-1's RLUSD/stablecoin basics. Verified current state of RLUSD as of June 2026: market cap ~$1.7-1.8B (8th-largest stablecoin, 3rd-largest US-regulated), up from ~$130M a year prior. It is NO LONGER an XRPL+Ethereum-only token -- a June 2026 expansion via Wormhole Native Token Transfers (NTT) added Base, Optimism, Ink, Unichain, and the XRPL EVM sidechain, but ~80-82% of supply circulates on Ethereum (ERC-20), NOT the XRP Ledger itself. On XRPL, RLUSD is a plain issued (IOU) fungible token requiring a trust line to Ripple's issuing account; its on-chain settings (verified from ripple/RLUSD-Implementation) enable lsfAllowTrustLineClawback, lsfGlobalFreeze (+ DeepFreeze capability), lsfDepositAuth, and lsfDefaultRipple -- meaning Ripple as issuer can freeze and claw back tokens to follow court orders. The single most load-bearing honesty point for a game builder: the parts that touch real fiat money -- minting against USD, redemption, the on/off ramp, and KYC -- are application-layer/custodial (Ripple, Brale, MoonPay, Uphold, exchanges), NOT XRPL protocol features. XRPL gives you fast/cheap settlement, native DEX/AMM swap between your soft currency and RLUSD, and issuer controls (freeze/clawback/authorized trust lines/transfer fee). It does NOT give you a regulated dollar, a bank, or a license. Regulatory reality hardened in 2026: the GENIUS Act took effect 2026-05-01, federalizing payment-stablecoin issuance (OCC + state option, 1:1 high-quality liquid reserves, BSA/AML, and a Sec 4(a)(11) ban on issuers paying yield to holders -- though affiliated platforms can still run reward programs). Paying players real value pulls you into money-transmitter / AML / (in some designs) gambling regimes, which is exactly where the identity-compliance track (DIDs, Credentials, authorized trust lines, deposit auth) earns its keep. Architecture takeaway for a studio: keep the in-game soft currency as your own XRPL IOU you fully control; peg/back the cash-out tier in RLUSD; never custody fiat yourself -- route mint/redeem and KYC through a regulated partner (Brale to issue your own branded coin and settle in RLUSD, or MoonPay/Uphold/exchanges for player ramps); gate real-value payouts behind verified identity. Tokenized real-world reward assets (treasuries, commodities, branded RWAs) are live and surging on XRPL (~$2.3-3B by mid-2026) but are issuer/custodian-gated and almost always permissioned, so treat them as a premium/loyalty rail with KYC, not an open in-game drop.

capabilities.name: RLUSD as in-game store of value / premium-currency backing
capabilities.summary: Using Ripple's regulated USD stablecoin as the hard-value anchor behind a game's premium currency, instead of pricing premium goods in a volatile coin or a pure off-chain ledger. On XRPL, RLUSD is an issued (IOU) fungible token: a player's wallet holds an RLUSD balance via a trust line to Ripple's issuing account, and your game can quote a 'gem'/'crystal' premium currency at a fixed RLUSD rate. Distinct from Wave-1's 'what is RLUSD' -- this is the design pattern of treating RLUSD as the settlement floor your premium economy is denominated in, so premium balances hold a real, redeemable dollar value rather than a floating one.
capabilities.key_fields: RLUSD is a plain XRPL IOU (not a special token type); requires a trust line to Ripple's XRPL issuing account to hold. Verified mid-2026: ~$1.7-1.8B market cap, 1:1 backed by USD deposits + short-term US Treasuries + cash equivalents; ~80-82% of supply on Ethereum, smaller share native on XRPL. Peg held via Ripple mint/redeem at $1, not an on-chain algorithm.
capabilities.gotchas: The peg and redeemability are an issuer promise enforced off-chain (reserves + GENIUS-Act-style regulation), NOT an XRPL protocol guarantee -- XRPL just moves the IOU. The MAJORITY of RLUSD lives on Ethereum, so if your players' RLUSD arrives from an exchange it may be ERC-20 and need bridging (Wormhole NTT) to reach XRPL. Holding RLUSD as 'store of value' for players does NOT let you, the game, pay them yield on it (GENIUS Act Sec 4(a)(11) bans issuer yield; affiliated reward programs are a separate, regulated matter). Backing premium currency in RLUSD makes that currency arguably real money -> compliance obligations attach (see identity-compliance capability).

best_for.purpose: Denominating a premium / hard currency in a stable, redeemable dollar value
Giving premium balances real-world worth players trust

capabilities.name: Player cash-in / cash-out (on-ramp / off-ramp) pattern
capabilities.summary: The end-to-end flow that converts a player's fiat (card/bank) into in-game value and back out to cash. On-ramp: player pays fiat to a regulated ramp provider (MoonPay, Uphold, an exchange), receives RLUSD into a wallet, then the game swaps RLUSD -> in-game currency (or credits a balance). Off-ramp (payout): game sends RLUSD to the player's wallet, player sells RLUSD for fiat via the same providers (bank transfer or Push-to-Card in 80+ countries). The ramp -- the actual fiat<->crypto step -- is ENTIRELY application-layer/custodial; XRPL only carries the RLUSD leg between the ramp and your game.
capabilities.key_fields: RLUSD ramp providers verified mid-2026: MoonPay (buy/sell, bank transfer + Push-to-Card payouts, 80+ countries), Uphold, Bitstamp, Bitso, Bullish, Independent Reserve, CoinMENA. Ripple Payments offers stablecoin payout + integrated off-ramp partners for paying contractors/employees in RLUSD with local-currency conversion. On-XRPL leg: standard Payment transactions of the RLUSD IOU; in-game swap can use the native DEX/AMM.
capabilities.gotchas: Every ramp does its own KYC -- you do NOT inherit it, and the player may be blocked by their jurisdiction even if your game allows them. Ramps charge spread + fees, so the dollar in is not the dollar out; design your prices around it. The on-ramp and off-ramp are separate licensed activities -- a provider that lets players BUY may not let them SELL in their country. If you ever take fiat directly instead of routing through a ramp, YOU become a money transmitter. RLUSD from an exchange is often ERC-20; getting it onto XRPL may require a bridge step the player doesn't understand.

capabilities.name: Stablecoin-pegged / stablecoin-backed in-game currency
capabilities.summary: Issuing your OWN game currency as an XRPL IOU and pegging or fully backing it to RLUSD, rather than handing players raw RLUSD. You control the token (name, transfer fee, freeze, authorized trust lines), while RLUSD is the reserve/redemption asset. Two flavors: (1) soft-peg -- a display/quoting peg where your token is just a points balance redeemable for RLUSD at a fixed rate at the cash-out boundary; (2) hard-backed -- you hold 1 RLUSD in reserve per unit minted and let players redeem on demand. The on-chain swap between your IOU and RLUSD can run on XRPL's native DEX/AMM, but the BACKING (holding the RLUSD reserve, honoring redemption) is your application-layer obligation.
capabilities.key_fields: Your token: a normal XRPL trust-line IOU you issue. Issuer controls available: TransferFee (built-in fee on secondary transfers), lsfGlobalFreeze / DeepFreeze, lsfAllowTrustLineClawback (must be set BEFORE issuance), RequireAuth (authorized trust lines) to whitelist holders, TickSize. Native DEX + AMM (XLS-30) can provide an on-ledger your-token<->RLUSD market. Redemption math: 1 unit = fixed RLUSD; reserve held off-chain or in a treasury wallet.
capabilities.gotchas: A token you can freeze/claw back/whitelist is the right call for a controlled game economy, but it is NOT decentralized money -- be honest with players. If you hard-back it, you are now custodying RLUSD against a redeemable liability, which can look like issuing a stablecoin yourself (potential GENIUS-Act/money-transmitter exposure) -- soft-peg points that are only redeemed at a regulated boundary is the safer default. lsfAllowTrustLineClawback can ONLY be enabled when the issuing account has issued nothing yet; retrofitting is impossible, so decide at genesis. An AMM pool exposes your peg to arbitrage and impermanent loss; a managed redemption desk avoids that but is centralized. RequireAuth means every player must be individually authorized -- great for compliance, heavy for onboarding.

capabilities.name: Settling player payouts in RLUSD over XRPL
capabilities.summary: Paying out real value to players (tournament prizes, creator/UGC revenue share, staking-style rewards, marketplace seller proceeds) by sending RLUSD over the XRP Ledger directly to player wallets, settling in seconds at sub-cent fees. This is the genuinely XRPL-native strength: the settlement rail. The payout itself is a standard RLUSD Payment transaction; what surrounds it (deciding eligibility, KYC-gating, tax reporting, the off-ramp the player uses afterward) is application-layer. Ripple's own contractor/employee payout flow is the same shape and a useful reference architecture.
capabilities.key_fields: Mechanism: Payment transaction of RLUSD IOU from a treasury wallet to the player's wallet (player must hold a trust line to Ripple's RLUSD issuer first). Settlement: seconds, ~3-4s ledger close; cost: fractions of a cent. Player must have an established RLUSD trust line OR you batch via a partner. Real-world precedent: Ripple Payments stablecoin payroll; XO Cash signing bonuses ($2,500 to 40 athletes, Mar 2026) show the instant-stablecoin-payout pattern (on a different rail).
capabilities.gotchas: You cannot push RLUSD to a wallet that has no trust line to the issuer -- the payment fails; either require players to set the trust line during onboarding or settle through a custodial wallet that already holds one. Paying real value triggers tax-reporting and (often) AML obligations on YOUR side; the seconds-fast rail does not absolve you of payee diligence. Reserve requirement: each new trust line costs the player 0.2 XRP reserve -- a UX speed bump for non-crypto users. If you must reverse a mistaken/fraudulent payout, you can only claw back YOUR OWN issued token, never RLUSD (you don't control Ripple's clawback) -- design a compensator before, not after.

capabilities.name: Issuer freeze & clawback controls for a real-value currency
capabilities.summary: The XRPL protocol-native toolkit that makes a real-value game currency operable under real-world rules: an issuer can freeze a holder's trust line (and DeepFreeze to also block incoming/outgoing), claw back issued tokens (Clawback amendment), and require authorization to hold the token (authorized trust lines). RLUSD itself runs with clawback + global/deep freeze + deposit auth enabled, specifically so Ripple can comply with court orders and law enforcement. For a studio issuing its own backed currency, these are the levers for fraud reversal, sanctioned-wallet freezing, and refund handling -- the on-chain half of a compliance program. Distinct from generic IOU mechanics: this is the deliberate compliance-control surface.
capabilities.key_fields: lsfAllowTrustLineClawback (Clawback amendment, enabled mainnet 2024) -- set at genesis only, lets issuer reclaim its own issued tokens. lsfGlobalFreeze + individual trust-line freeze; DeepFreeze (XLS-77d) enabled 2025 adds the ability to freeze a line so the holder cannot move funds at all. RequireAuth (authorized trust lines) whitelists holders. lsfDepositAuth restricts who can pay the issuer. These apply to YOUR issued token; you have NO such power over RLUSD (Ripple does).
capabilities.gotchas: Clawback and NoFreeze are mutually exclusive and both must be decided BEFORE you issue -- you cannot add clawback later, and you cannot remove NoFreeze once set. Freeze/clawback are blunt and centralized; over-using them destroys player trust and contradicts 'real ownership' marketing -- reserve for fraud/legal, document the policy. Freeze does NOT delete the balance, it immobilizes it; clawback actually removes it. You can freeze/claw back ONLY tokens you issued -- a game cannot freeze a player's RLUSD or XRP. Authorized trust lines add onboarding friction (each holder needs a TrustSet authorization tx from the issuer).
