capabilities.name: Regulatory & compliance reality of paying players real value
capabilities.summary: The honest compliance picture: the moment your game lets players turn play into withdrawable dollars, you stop being just a game and touch money-transmission, AML/KYC, tax, securities, and (for chance-based reward designs) gambling law. None of this is solved by XRPL -- it is the application-layer obligation that the identity-compliance track exists to satisfy on-chain (DIDs, Credentials, authorized trust lines, deposit auth gating who can receive real value). Verified 2026 anchors: the GENIUS Act took effect 2026-05-01 (federal payment-stablecoin framework: OCC + state option, 1:1 high-quality liquid reserves, BSA/AML, and Sec 4(a)(11) banning issuers from paying yield to holders); EU MiCA and APAC regimes (Singapore MAS, Hong Kong) add jurisdictional patchwork. This is a capability because designing around it (who you pay, after what verification) is a first-class architecture decision, not legal boilerplate.
capabilities.key_fields: GENIUS Act effective 2026-05-01; defines 'payment stablecoin' (redeemable for fixed monetary value, stable-value representation); requires 1:1 cash/cash-equivalent reserves; issuers must comply with the Bank Secrecy Act for AML. Sec 4(a)(11): no issuer-paid yield to holders (affiliated platform reward programs are separately regulated, not outright banned). Real-money gaming/iGaming: regulators treat real-money platforms as financial institutions for AML; KYC verification triggers on payout thresholds. MiCA (EU) + MAS (Singapore) + HK Ordinance = multi-jurisdiction obligations.
capabilities.gotchas: If you ever hold player fiat or convert it yourself, you are likely a money transmitter (state-by-state in the US, license per jurisdiction) -- routing through a regulated ramp/issuer is what keeps you out of that. Chance-based loot purchased with, or convertible to, real money can be GAMBLING in many jurisdictions even if you call it a game. Issuing your own RLUSD-redeemable currency can put YOU inside the payment-stablecoin definition -- soft-peg points redeemed only at a regulated boundary is the safer pattern. Compliance is jurisdictional: a payout flow legal in one country can be illegal in the player's. AML diligence is on the payer -- the fast XRPL rail does not transfer that duty to Ripple.

Settles RLUSD across XRPL + Ethereum. Uses XRPL Authorized Trust Lines (restrict holders to approved accounts) + freeze controls. Authorized-trust-line gating means your players must be approved holders, adding onboarding friction (good for compliance, a UX cost). A branded coin still sits inside the GENIUS-Act payment-stablecoin perimeter -- you're relying on Brale's permits, so your design choices are constrained by their compliance program. capabilities.name: Tokenized real-world reward assets on XRPL
capabilities.summary: Using tokenized real-world assets (RWAs) -- tokenized US Treasuries, money-market funds, commodities, or branded reward assets -- as premium/loyalty rewards that carry actual off-chain value, beyond a cosmetic NFT. XRPL's RWA tokenization surged in 2025-2026 (~$2.3-3B on-ledger by mid-2026, up from ~$25M in early 2025), backed by Ripple Custody and partners like Archax, Ondo, and major banks. For a game, an RWA reward (e.g., a yield-bearing tokenized-treasury voucher as a season prize) is real value players can redeem. But RWAs are issuer/custodian-gated and almost always PERMISSIONED -- this is the most application-layer, least DIY capability in the lane, hence the low builder_fit.
capabilities.key_fields: XRPL RWA total ~$2.3B mid-2026 (some coverage cites ~$3B), from ~$25M Jan 2025 -- a >2,200% 2025 surge driven by post-SEC-resolution regulatory clarity and Ripple Custody. Live asset types: tokenized US Treasuries, money-market funds, commodities. Notable: Ondo/JPMorgan/Mastercard/Ripple completed a cross-institution tokenized-Treasury redemption in <5s. Issuance/custody via Ripple Custody + Archax (targeting $1B+ by mid-2026). Almost all permissioned (authorized trust lines, accredited/KYC'd holders).
capabilities.gotchas: RWAs are NOT open in-game drops -- holders are typically KYC'd/accredited and the token is permissioned, so you cannot freely airdrop a tokenized Treasury to anonymous players. The off-chain value depends entirely on the issuer/custodian honoring it -- counterparty risk, not protocol guarantee. Securities law attaches fast: a yield-bearing tokenized asset given as a reward can be an unregistered securities offering depending on structure/jurisdiction. Redemption is gated by the issuer's process, not instant like RLUSD. Lowest builder_fit in the lane: powerful for a premium loyalty tier with a regulated partner, wrong tool for everyday game rewards (use NFTs for cosmetics, RLUSD for cash value).

capabilities.name: Multi-chain RLUSD liquidity & XRPL EVM bridging
capabilities.summary: The reality that RLUSD is now multi-chain and that a game economy must plan for where its players' dollars actually live. A June 2026 expansion via Wormhole Native Token Transfers (NTT) extended RLUSD beyond XRPL + Ethereum to Base, Optimism, Ink, Unichain, and the XRPL EVM sidechain -- moving real (not synthetic) tokens between chains. Since ~80-82% of RLUSD circulates on Ethereum, players funding via an exchange often hold ERC-20 RLUSD that must be bridged to reach the XRP Ledger (Axelar bridges XRPL mainnet <-> XRPL EVM sidechain). For a studio this is mostly a UX/routing concern: decide which chain your economy settles on and how players' RLUSD arrives there. Low builder_fit -- important context, but bridging is plumbing you mostly delegate to ramps/wallets, not a feature you build into the game loop.
capabilities.key_fields: RLUSD networks mid-2026: XRPL (IOU), Ethereum (ERC-20, ~80-82% of supply), + Base, Optimism, Ink, Unichain, XRPL EVM sidechain. Cross-chain mechanism: Wormhole Native Token Transfers (NTT) -- native, not wrapped/synthetic. XRPL EVM sidechain live on mainnet 2025-06-30 (Cosmos SDK + EVM, ~1,000 TPS); Axelar is the bridge between XRPL mainnet and the EVM sidechain (connecting 80+ chains). RLUSD on XRPL = trust-line IOU; on EVM chains = ERC-20.
capabilities.gotchas: Bridging adds steps, fees, and failure modes most non-crypto players cannot navigate -- if your economy settles on XRPL but players' RLUSD is ERC-20, you (or your ramp/wallet) must abstract the bridge entirely. The XRPL EVM sidechain is a SEPARATE chain from XRPL mainnet -- smart-contract RLUSD there is not the same balance as your mainnet IOU; don't conflate them. Bridge security is a real attack surface (cross-chain bridges are historically the highest-value exploit target) -- prefer routing through reputable ramps over asking players to self-bridge. Because most liquidity is on Ethereum, deep on-XRPL RLUSD liquidity for large payouts may be thinner than headline market cap suggests.
